title: Add no-placeholder task registry and acceptance gate

context.summary: Register the public-readiness remediation tasks and add an executable gate that tracks every current temporary or incomplete public path to a concrete task.
context.background: The repository is a local MVP, but public readiness now requires every supported and experimental path to have real implementation rather than untracked temporary markers.

in: Create task files for TASK-87 through TASK-113.
Update tasks/tasks.json so TASK-87 is the current completed task and TASK-88 through TASK-113 are registered drafts.
Add a validation script that scans public/runtime paths for temporary or incomplete markers.
Require every current marker to be owned by a concrete future task and fail if new untracked markers are introduced.
Wire the new validation into pnpm check.
out: Implementing Qdrant, Docling, sync antivirus, LLM providers, observability, backup, release, update or Hermes runtime features.
Removing current public-readiness debt; follow-up tasks own the actual removals.

acceptance_criteria: tasks/tasks.json registers TASK-87 through TASK-113 with valid TASK IDs and task files.
TASK-87 is marked done and TASK-88 through TASK-113 remain draft until executed individually.
The new validation gate maps every current marker to a concrete future task.
The validation gate fails if an untracked temporary marker appears in scanned runtime or public documentation paths.
The validation gate fails for a task-owned marker once that owner task is marked done and the marker still remains.

manual_checks: Confirm no product runtime implementation is changed by this task.
Confirm every follow-up task has a concrete implementation acceptance criterion rather than a blocking-only fallback.

risks: A strict gate can make later work noisy if it is not tied to task ownership.
A loose gate would allow new temporary markers to appear without an owner.
definition_of_done: Task status is changed to done.
Branch is committed and merged back into master.
